policy: A flag states that no official source confirms a value, or that a committed artefact disagrees with one. Flags do not block a merge; they are published here with the link that settles them.

rows.what: The results feed in the repository (data/s9cb/games.csv) is 12 games behind the official schedule. It was fetched 2026-11-15 13:21 UTC, before the Week 10 Sunday kickoffs, so it holds 1 of 14 Week-10 results and standings recomputed from it reproduce only 8 of 32 clubs.
rows.why_it_matters: Any ROI, rating or closing-line number computed from the feed today describes Week 9 plus the Thursday game.
rows.what_settles_it: Refresh the feed, then re-run console/verify.py. The check prints the gap between the last final in the feed and the last final on the official schedule page.

rows.what: Injury captures carry a date but no clock time, and hold rendered text rather than the bytes we read.
rows.why_it_matters: Two reads on the same day cannot be ordered, and a transcription cannot be re-audited against the page.
rows.what_settles_it: Store the raw response with a timestamp including time of day and time zone, per capture.

rows.what: nfl.com prints AZ for the Arizona Cardinals and LA for the Los Angeles Rams; the repository stores both AZ/ARI and LA/LAR in different files.
rows.why_it_matters: Every join between two files is exposed to a silent mismatch.
rows.what_settles_it: One alias table enforced at build time; the build fails on an unknown code.

rows.what: data/standings.json records Buffalo at 7-1 (retrieved 2026-11-12). The official table today records 8-1.
rows.why_it_matters: At least one published page shows a table that is four days and two game weeks out of date.
rows.what_settles_it: Regenerate from the official table, or mark the file historical and point readers at the current capture.

rows.what: The Week 11 injury report is not published. https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 serves the Week 10 page, with the week selector offering Week 1 to Week 10 only.
rows.why_it_matters: There is no official forward-looking availability data for Week 11 today, so no Week-11 line can carry an injury feature.
rows.what_settles_it: Re-read the URL on Wednesday; the first read whose title says Week 11 is the boundary.

rows.what: The Week 10 injury report is still live on the Monday after the games, with its designations intact.
rows.why_it_matters: A reader, or a model, can mistake a record of what was known before Week 10 for a forecast about Week 11.
rows.what_settles_it: Stamp every published injury row with the week it describes and the week it can be used for.

rows.what: No venue has been transcribed from an official game-centre page. The stadium column in the results feed comes from a parsed copy of the schedule, not from the league's own game centre.
rows.why_it_matters: One brief line is unmet, and the roof/surface overlay has no official foundation.
rows.what_settles_it: Read one week of game-centre pages by hand; if the venue is in the text, automate it.

rows.what: Seven pull requests from other sessions are open against main. This session did not merge them.
rows.why_it_matters: The site carries several generations of pages and the numbers on them are not guaranteed to agree.
rows.what_settles_it: An integration session merges them and re-verifies the combined data line by line.

rows.what: Myles Garrett appears in the Los Angeles Rams section of the official Week 10 injury report, which looks like a mis-scrape.
rows.why_it_matters: If it were a scrape error, every Rams row would be suspect.
rows.what_settles_it: Re-read on 2026-11-16: the official page itself lists him under the Rams, with 'Knee, Not injury related - resting player'. Not an error in the capture.

rows.what: The committed 2026-11-15 injury capture is a transcription, so it could differ from the official page.
rows.why_it_matters: Every injury number on the site depends on it.
rows.what_settles_it: Re-read the whole page on 2026-11-16 and compared row by row: 347 rows against 347, 0 rows only in one side, 0 field differences, and the sha256 of this session's capture equals the hash recorded in data/capture/manifest.json (9fe77d36...cd5f). The capture is faithful.

rows.what: The official standings table could contain arithmetic the league itself disagrees with, as it has in earlier weeks.
rows.why_it_matters: A derived metric built on a self-contradictory cell would be wrong in a way no downstream check would catch.
rows.what_settles_it: Checked on 2026-11-16: total wins equal total losses at 148 each, and total points for equal total points against at 6,880. The table is internally consistent.
